b1.note: SharedArrayBuffer requires both Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin AND Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (or credentialless) to be set on the document response. Both headers are required; isolation is a logical AND.

b2.verdict: disagree: timestamp-query is an OPTIONAL feature in Chrome — it is NOT exposed by default in the sense that the developer must (a) request 'timestamp-query' when calling requestDevice() and (b) the WebGPU Developer Features flag (chrome://flags/#enable-webgpu-developer-features) is required to disable 100μs quantization. The feature does NOT work at full precision for ordinary web content without enabling this flag. Note: the feature is available to non-isolated contexts (the earlier plan to restrict it was revised).
b2.note: The feature itself is implemented and available, but (a) it must be explicitly requested via requiredFeatures: ['timestamp-query'], and (b) without the WebGPU Developer Features flag the values are quantized to 100μs. Chrome developer docs explicitly state the flag is required: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/webgpu/developer-features

b3.note: The failure occurs when the Wasm module tries to instantiate a WebAssembly.Memory with shared:true or spawn a Worker that uses SharedArrayBuffer — at that point SharedArrayBuffer is undefined and the module throws. Module structure validation may pass; the failure manifests at instantiation time. The practical effect is the same: the threaded Wasm module fails to load without cross-origin isolation.
